original_value: AbstractIn this work we introduce and analyze a new and comprehensive multilayer dataset covering a wide spectrum of international relationships between coutries. We select two cross sections of the dataset corresponding to years 2003 and 2010 with 19 layers and 112 nodes to study the structure and evolution of the network. Country centrality is measured by the multiplex PageRank (MultiRank) and the multiplex hub and authority scores (MultiHub and MultiAuth). We find that the MultiHub measure has the highest correlation to GDP per capita, with respect to the other multilayer measures and to their single layer analogues. Finally we analyze the differences in the ranking between GDP per capita and the multilayer centrality measures to evaluate them as measures of development.

result.paraphrase: This study presents and examines a new, comprehensive multilayer dataset spanning a broad range of international relationships between countries. Two cross sections, from 2003 and 2010, are used to investigate the network’s structure and evolution, each with 19 layers and 112 nodes. Country centrality is assessed through multiplex PageRank (MultiRank) and multiplex hub and authority scores (MultiHub and MultiAuth). The results show that MultiHub correlates most strongly with GDP per capita, compared with the other multilayer measures and their single-layer counterparts. The paper also studies ranking differences between GDP per capita and the multilayer centrality measures to assess their value as development indicators.
